evidence.quote: The Ti-Nb-Hf shape memory alloys with various Hf contents were composed of the α ´´ martensite phase and β phase, regardless of Hf contents.

other.remelting: repeatedly melted at least six times

evidence.quote: were prepared by arc melting at an Ar atmosphere from higher purity Ti (99.9 5wt.%), Nb (99.95 wt.%) and Hf (99.92 wt.%). To achieve compositional homoge - neity, the Ti-Nb-Hf alloy ingots were repeatedly melted at least six times.
The present Ti-Nb-Hf alloy ingots were homogenized at 850 ◦ C for 6 h
and then hot-rolled into sheets with a thickness of 3 mm.
the hot-rolled Ti-Nb-Hf sheets were heat treated at 850 ◦ C for 1 h
followed by cold rolling with a reduction of 70%
the specimens with the moderate standards were encapsulated in sealed quartz tubes under the protection of Ar and solution treated at 900 ◦ C for 3 h.

conditions.test_method: DMA, single cantilever clamp, step heating, frequency 0.5 Hz, oscillation amplitude 0.05%

evidence.quote: the maximum damping capacity of 0.0236 can be optimized by controlling the Hf content in Ti-Nb-Hf shape memory alloys.
A higher strength and larger recoverable strain can be obtained in Ti- Nb shape memory alloy modified by 2 at.% Hf due to grain refinement, precipitation strengthening and solution strengthening.
